title: White chocolate cranberry bark
subtitle: white chocolate bark with dried cranberry and pistachio
excerpt: White chocolate cranberry bark is a thin, set slab of melted white chocolate scattered with dried cranberries, chopped pistachios, and a little flaky sea salt. It's bright, tart, sweet, and crunchy, and takes about 15 minutes to make. Broken into shards and boxed up, it makes a good gift or a useful addition to a Christmas sweet plate.
sourceNotes: White chocolate bark became popular as a home confectionery project in the 2000s, following the same format as dark chocolate bark, thin poured slabs with contrasting toppings. The cranberry and pistachio combination, with its Christmas colour palette of red and green on white, became particularly widespread as a festive gift-food item. White chocolate is made from cocoa butter, milk solids, and sugar with no cocoa mass, giving a sweeter, creamier base that pairs well with tart or salty toppings.

content.text: White chocolate cranberry bark is a thin snappable slab of white chocolate covered in tart dried cranberries and crunchy pistachios. It looks festive, tastes bright and sweet, and is actually one of the simplest confectionery projects. White chocolate burns easily at high heat, keep the temperature gentle.

Put the chopped white chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water. The base of the bowl must not touch the water. Stir gently and frequently. White chocolate is more prone to seizing and scorching than dark; keep the heat very low and remove the bowl from the heat as soon as the last lumps have melted. Stir until completely smooth.

Line a large baking tray with parchment paper. Pour the melted chocolate onto the tray and spread it to an even layer about 4 mm thick using a palette knife or the back of a spoon. Scatter the dried cranberries, chopped pistachios, and sea salt flakes evenly over the surface. Press the toppings very gently into the chocolate so they adhere when it sets.

Refrigerate for 1 hour until completely firm. Lift onto a board and break into shards by hand along natural fault lines. Store in an airtight container in a cool spot, not the fridge once broken, as condensation causes the surface to spot. It keeps for up to 3 weeks.
